question: Represent all one-, two-, and three-dimensional Bravais lattices through factored dimension-specific lattice-system enums plus P/C/I/F/R centering, or through one concrete class per Bravais combination?

options.summary: Use dimension-specific lattice-system types plus one P/C/I/F/R centering type and validated Bravais system-centering records.
options.consequence: The public API represents all 1D, 2D, and 3D Bravais combinations without twenty duplicative concrete classes; direct/reciprocal duality and metric compatibility remain separate analyzers.

options.summary: Create one concrete public class for each Bravais lattice combination.
options.consequence: Every Bravais combination has a nominal runtime class at the cost of duplicated invariants, larger public surface, and more expensive extension and maintenance.

recommendation: FACTORED_SYSTEM_CENTERING_TYPES because P/C/I/F/R centering is orthogonal to lattice system, all allowed combinations remain explicit, and separate analyzers can own tolerance-dependent duality and metric compatibility.
blocked_scope: Calculation execution, accepted-parent reads, metric-classification tolerances not fixed by an accepted contract, multi-orbital or spin generalization, composite-degeneracy work, dependency changes, release, publication, commit, push, and automatic successor activation remain unauthorized.
safe_scope: Implement dimension-specific Lattice, DirectLattice, ReciprocalLattice, lattice-system, Bravais-centering, and validated Bravais system-centering records in ksdft2effmass.solid_state; implement exact represented duality analysis where its tolerance is an explicit caller input; add bounded software verification and public documentation.
authorized_scope: Implement dimension-specific Lattice, DirectLattice, ReciprocalLattice, lattice-system, Bravais-centering, and validated Bravais system-centering records in ksdft2effmass.solid_state; implement exact represented duality analysis where its tolerance is an explicit caller input; add bounded software verification and public documentation.
